evidence.note: Systematic section-by-section RFC reading (frame header, blocks, FSE §4.1.1, Huffman §4.2, sequences, Appendix A) before implementing, interleaved with hex dumps of real frames (simple.zst, img.png.zst); step 27 decodes simple.zst's header field-by-field from actual bytes.
Decodes literal-section-header byte 0x40 bit-by-bit against observed bytes, correcting an earlier misreading of the type/size_format bit layout — cross-checking spec against a real frame.

Traces real initial FSE states (LL=29, Off=26, ML=31) from repetitive.zst and compares the state→symbol mapping to RFC Appendix A (state 26 should map to sym 16, not 10), diagnosing a table-construction misread against ground-truth bytes.
Ties FSE-construction bugs to exact RFC clauses: '-1 symbols scanned in natural order' and the spreading step formula (tableSize>>1)+(tableSize>>3)+3, showing clause-level extraction of tricky rules.
Repeated but somewhat circular FSE debugging with multiple incorrect hardcoded-table transcriptions shows the up-front FSE model was NOT precise/verified, keeping it below the level-10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent works the RFC systematically section by section before each subsystem, extracts exact rules for the tricky areas (FSE construction, offset formula, literal-header bit layout), and repeatedly cross-checks them against hex dumps and traced values from real frames (steps 27, 58, 68) — the defining behavior of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 9-10 because the FSE spreading algorithm was genuinely mis-read up front and required many chaotic debugging rounds and wrong table transcriptions to reconcile, rather than a precise verified model documented in advance.
